newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures settle higher in technical correction.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures settle higher in technical correction.

text.p: FCOJ futures retraced recent losses and closed sharply firmer on technically-driven fund buying mixed with light buying by the trade, dealers said.
A lack of selling eased the move higher, they added.

The spot-March contract was seen trading in broad range between 84.00 and 90.00 cents. Prices are likely to stay within these boundaries until the U.S. Department of Agriculture issues its supply and demand report Feb 12.
The market awaits the report, which will include losses to Florida's crop from the Jan 19 freeze.

The expiry of March FCOJ after Friday's close could play a role in the market's activity over the next two days, analysts said. One analyst cited about 6,800 open put options with open interest at 15,117 lots in the March contract.
The spot month settled 2.40 higher at 86.55 cents, having ranged from 87.70 to 84.30 cents. The deferred contracts ended 2.55 to 1.05 higher.

The market will continue to monitor an Arctic air mass that could hit Florida by next Friday. At this point, the cold air is not likely to harm fruit, but low temperatures could stun new growth on the trees that lost foliage in the Jan 19 freeze, Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said.
"This new growth, which occurred because of the freeze, is now very vulnerable to low temperatures and adverse weather from this point on," Davis said.
He said it is too soon to predict how far the barameter could drop.
